summary: Iteration 7 — Time-Off Self-Service. Added /app/backend/tests/test_time_off.py with 17 tests inside a single TestTimeOff class (xdist loadscope-pinned). All 17 new tests pass and full backend suite (84/84) is green including all iteration 3/4/5/6 regressions. Covered: valid create (200 pending, full response shape), end<start (400 'End date is before start date'), past start (400 'Cannot request time off in the past'), overlap (400 'You already have a request covering those dates'), owner-cannot-create (403), employee /me listing, admin list + ?status=pending filter, cross-org tenant isolation via fresh register-org owner (foreign list is empty), approve flow + double-approve 400 'Request is already approved' + audit-log row action='time_off.approved', deny flow + audit 'time_off.denied' + double-deny 400, SCHEDULE OVERRIDE: pending time-off does NOT block /sessions/start (200), APPROVED time-off blocks with 403 detail 'Approved time off today (<reason>). Enjoy your day.' including exact reason substring 'sick day' and 'Enjoy your day', stacking: weekly_calendar OPEN NOW + approved time-off → 403 reason contains time-off reason ('wedding') and not 'shift', GET /time-off/today returns null when pending or none, returns approved doc when covering today, employee DELETE own PENDING → 200, DELETE own APPROVED → 400 'Only pending requests can be cancelled', DELETE another employee's request → 403 'Not your request', 404 on non-existent id for approve/deny/delete. Teardown deletes ALL time_off_requests rows via admin GET+DELETE, resets employee schedule to {mode:'any'}, deletes test office, and resets any active session.

minor.issue: When there is no approved time-off, endpoint returns HTTP 200 with a null JSON body. Spec allows this ('null or 200 with null body'), but some HTTP clients treat body=null as empty; consider returning {} or explicit {status:'none'} for consumer ergonomics.
No pagination — a busy org could get an unbounded list. Consider ?limit/skip once volume grows.

critical_code_review_comments: routes/time_off.py::_decide uses f-string in detail 'Request is already {status}' which matches the spec exactly, good. But the double-approve message hard-codes 'approved' even if the record was DENIED then someone calls approve — currently it says 'Request is already denied', which is correct wording but potentially confusing UX (client expected 400 'already approved'). Consider distinguishing 'Cannot approve a denied request'.

routes/time_off.py overlap check uses status $in ['pending','approved'] — good — but does not consider a denied request; if an employee gets denied they can immediately re-submit an identical window. Product may want a small cool-down or explicit re-request semantics.

routes/time_off.py::cancel_request lets admins delete APPROVED time-off, which is destructive and skips audit logging. Recommend: log_admin_action for admin deletes of time-off, and require an 'admin_override' flag when deleting an approved doc (to avoid silent revocation of already-taken leave).

routes/sessions.py::_compute_schedule_duration_ms — time-off UTC-date comparison uses `datetime.now(timezone.utc).date().isoformat()`, but the employee schedule uses per-employee `timezone`. An approved time-off spanning today UTC may not cover 'today' in employee's local TZ near midnight boundaries. Consider using the schedule.timezone for the today lookup to keep semantics consistent with the weekly_calendar path.

models.py::TimeOffCreate has regex date pattern but no calendar-date validation (e.g. '2025-13-40' passes regex). Add a field_validator that parses via date.fromisoformat to reject malformed real dates.
TimeOffCreate.reason min_length=1 allows a single space (Pydantic min_length checks raw length before strip). Add validator to reject whitespace-only reasons.

Carried from prior iterations: (a) overnight shifts still return 'Invalid schedule: close time is before open time.', (b) EmployeeSchedule allows a fully-null weekly_schedule map (mode+timezone but no days), (c) bad IANA tz silently downgrades to UTC in sessions.py despite model validation — mismatch.
